title: Access to Justice (Civil Litigation Reforms) Amendment Bill 2009

speeches.speaker: Joe Ludwig
speeches.brief: The speaker moved that the bills be taken together, proceed without formalities, and be read a first time, and indicated that after the second reading debate is adjourned, a motion will be made to list them separately on the Notice Paper. The motions were agreed to and the bills were read a first time.

speeches.speaker: Joe Ludwig
speeches.brief: Three bills were introduced for a second reading: the Access to Justice (Civil Litigation Reforms) Amendment Bill 2009, which strengthens Federal Court case management, appeals, and judicial responsibilities to cut litigation costs (citing the $200 million C7 case and $6.2 million Bell case, with parties paying under 15%); the National Health Security Amendment Bill 2009, which extends security-sensitive biological agent (SSBA) rules to suspected agents, adds search and seizure warrants, and requires police reports; and the Offshore Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage (Safety Levies) Amendment Bill 2009, which replaces the pipeline safety management plan levy with a safety case levy from 1 January 2010.

speeches.speaker: Mark Furner
speeches.brief: Presented the Legal and Constitutional Affairs Legislation Committee report on the Access to Justice (Civil Litigation Reforms) Amendment Bill 2009.

speeches.speaker: Steve Hutchins
speeches.brief: Senator Abetz argued that the Access to Justice (Civil Litigation Reforms) Amendment Bill 2009 introduces case management reforms to reduce costs and delays, including an overarching purpose of just resolution, costs orders against lawyers, and alternative dispute resolution. He announced a coalition-supported amendment, co-sponsored with Senator Bob Brown, to require a full-time Federal Court registrar in Hobart.

speeches.speaker: Penny Wong
speeches.brief: Government amendments were moved to delete paragraphs that would have removed the right to appeal interlocutory decisions on security for costs, and to allow Federal Court judges (other than the Chief Justice) to hold concurrent appointments on state supreme courts. An additional amendment requiring a full-time registrar in each state’s Federal Court registry, including Hobart, was also agreed to.

The House of Representatives agreed to Senate amendments 1–5 of the Access to Justice (Civil Litigation Reforms) Amendment Bill 2009, disagreed to amendment 6 but substituted its own amendment, and requested Senate reconsideration and concurrence. The Senate ordered the message be considered in Committee of the Whole immediately.

speeches.speaker: Nick Sherry
speeches.brief: The speaker moved to accept a House amendment replacing Senate amendment no. 6 to the Access to Justice (Civil Litigation Reforms) Amendment Bill 2009, which introduces a proportionate cost and case management framework for federal courts. The speaker also welcomed the government's concession to restore a full-time registrar in the Tasmanian District Registry of the Federal Court, reversing a previous cost-cutting measure.
